entry.title: Found the Leak: They Didn't Want the Flower to Wilk
entry.content:
In There’s a Leak in the Dyke, we counted seven dark money vehicles formed by one Dykema Gossett attorney. We traced the compliance team. We found the five levels. We said the dyke was leaking.

We didn’t know where the leak was.

Now we do.

The 990-EZ

Every tax-exempt organization files a return with the IRS. Form 990 for the large ones. Form 990-EZ for the small. The filer enters its name, its mission, its revenue, its expenses.

And on page 4, under Part IV — “List of Officers, Directors, Trustees, and Key Employees” — it names the person who prepared the form.

For Save Detroit Jobs, tax year 2023, that person is Olivia RC A Flower.

Flower works at Dykema Gossett’s Ann Arbor office.

Save Detroit Jobs was incorporated by W. Alan Wilk, who works at Dykema Gossett’s Lansing office.

Save Detroit Jobs is governed by Renae Moore, who works at Dykema Gossett’s Lansing office.

Three employees. Two offices. One vehicle.

Why Ann Arbor?

Dykema Gossett operates from five Michigan offices: Detroit, Lansing, Ann Arbor, Grand Rapids, and Bloomfield Hills. The political compliance team — Wilk’s team — is headquartered in Lansing. Phone extensions 9121 and 9122, one digit apart.

If the formation is in Lansing, and the governance is in Lansing, why is the tax filing in Ann Arbor?

The answer is on Dykema’s own website. Their Ann Arbor office lists among its practice areas: Tax. The firm routes its tax compliance work to Ann Arbor. This is normal law firm architecture — specialized teams handle specialized work regardless of which office originated the client.

But it means the paperwork trail crosses offices. The formation attorney in Lansing hands the vehicle to the tax specialist in Ann Arbor, who files the 990-EZ with the IRS, which becomes a public record, which names the preparer.

The 990-EZ is the leak. The preparer field is the drip. One name — Olivia RC A Flower — connects two offices that were never supposed to be connected on paper.

Eleven Vehicles

When we published the first article in October 2026, we counted seven Wilk vehicles from LARA records and campaign finance filings. Since then, independent reporting and public records have revealed four more.

#EntityYearSource
1Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders2016LARA
2Our Neighborhoods First2016LARA
3Detroit Jobs First2016LARA
4RFFW LLC2022LARA
5Put Progress First2023LARA
6Michigan First Principles2025LARA
7Peninsula Fundpre-2018LARA, testimony
8Progress Can’t WaitAug 2025LARA, Metro Times
9Blue Mitten ActionJun 17, 2026LARA, Metro Times
10Michiganders for Progressive Values FundSep 2024LARA
11Working For Michigan’s Future2007LARA

Seven became eleven. The formation velocity is accelerating.

Between 2007 and 2022, Wilk formed approximately one vehicle every two to three years. Since 2023, he has formed four in three years. The biennial burst pattern has become continuous.

Vehicles #8 and #9 were independently confirmed by Metro Times reporting. We did not tip them. They found the same nodes by following the same public records. When independent journalists arrive at the same data points through independent methods, the pattern is not inference. It is convergence.

The Formation-Governance Split

Here is the pattern across all known vehicles:

EntityWilk’s RoleMoore’s Role
Save Detroit JobsIncorporatorAssistant Secretary/Governance
Our Neighborhoods FirstIncorporatorGovernance
Detroit Jobs FirstIncorporatorGovernance
RFFW LLCIncorporatorGovernance
Peninsula FundIncorporatorGovernance
Turn Around Wayne County PACFormationRecord Keeper
Michiganders for Progressive Values FundIncorporator + Registered Agent—
Progress Can’t WaitIncorporator—
Blue Mitten ActionIncorporator—

At every vehicle where both names appear: Wilk forms. Moore governs. The same division. The same two people. The same employer.

Neither person does both. Wilk never governs. Moore never incorporates. The division is absolute. The plausible deniability is architectural — no single person controls the full lifecycle of any vehicle.

But together, they are the lifecycle.

Moore testified under oath in the Chatfield case that she manages more than 80 accounts at Dykema. She was the assistant secretary/treasurer of Chatfield’s Peninsula Fund — a Wilk formation. She serves the same role on Attorney General Dana Nessel’s Promise to the People Fund. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. Same desk. Same person.

And now, through the 990-EZ filing, we see the third node: Flower in Ann Arbor, filing the tax returns for the vehicles that Wilk forms and Moore governs.

Three roles. Three people. Two offices. One machine.

What This Means for the Schools

Save Detroit Jobs spent $84,000 in 2016 to defeat sitting Detroit City Council member Raquel Castañeda-López and elect her replacement. That replacement — Latisha Johnson — joined the board of Purpose Charter Academy, a school run by a superintendent with nine criminal convictions.

The same law firm that authored Michigan’s charter school legislation in the 1990s now forms the dark money vehicles that influence who sits on charter school boards. And the tax filings for those vehicles are prepared by a third employee at a third office.

The connection runs from Ann Arbor (tax filing) to Lansing (formation and governance) to Detroit (the council seat, the charter school, the nine-conviction superintendent).

One firm. Three offices. The full circuit.

The Agent Selection

In the first seven vehicles, Wilk used Corporation Company as the registered agent — a professional service that provides a buffer between the incorporator and the public filing.

For vehicle #10 — Michiganders for Progressive Values Fund, incorporated September 2024 — Wilk named himself as registered agent. No Corporation Company. No buffer. No membrane between the attorney and the entity.

Why drop the buffer for this one?

We don’t know. But the pattern shift is structural. It suggests either increased urgency (no time for Corporation Company setup), increased confidence (no perceived risk), or a different purpose for this vehicle that doesn’t require the same distance.

The agent selection is itself a data point. When the architect removes his own buffer, the architecture is speaking.

The Leak

In plumbing, a leak doesn’t just release water. It reveals pressure. Something inside the system is pushing outward against the seams. The water finds the weakest joint. The drip tells you which pipe is under stress.

The 990-EZ naming Olivia Flower is a drip. It tells you the cross-office pipe is under pressure — that the Lansing formation machine needs Ann Arbor’s tax infrastructure to complete the circuit. The drip wasn’t supposed to be visible. Tax preparers on 990-EZ filings are public record, but no one was supposed to look.

Someone looked.

The flower didn’t want to wilk. But the filing is public. The connection is made. And the dyke — the wall between the formation office and the tax office, between the political compliance team and the financial compliance team, between Lansing and Ann Arbor — has one more crack.

Eleven vehicles. Three employees. Two offices. One crack at a time.

Source Registry

Every claim in this article resolves to public record:

  • Olivia RC A Flower — Listed as 990-EZ preparer on Save Detroit Jobs tax filing, TY2023. Available via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer or IRS TEOS.
  • W. Alan Wilk — LARA entity search. Incorporator on all listed vehicles. Dykema biography: dykema.com/people/w-alan-wilk
  • Renae Moore — Sworn testimony in People v. Chatfield (Ingham County District Court, Feb 26, 2025). Dykema biography: dykema.com/people/renae-a-moore
  • Vehicle formations — Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) entity search
  • Save Detroit Jobs spending — Michigan Secretary of State Campaign Finance Reporting System (CFRS)
  • Metro Times confirmation — Independent reporting, 2026
  • Dykema Ann Arbor — dykema.com/offices/ann-arbor
  • Dykema charter school history — Quoted from firm’s own education practice page

Cross-reference:

  • There’s a Leak in the Dyke — the original: 7 vehicles, Moore’s testimony, 5 levels
  • The Corporate Network — LARA entity documentation
  • lansing.primals.eco — the capital infrastructure kernel
  • barry.primals.eco — statewide political infrastructure

entry.title: The Dykema Chronology — 1988 to Present
entry.content:
How to Read This

Every entry has a date, a source, and the actors/entities involved. The timeline traces one law firm’s connections across 36 years — from shelf corporations in 1988 to charter school board governance in 2026.

This is not a conspiracy theory. It is a public record.

Phase 1: Building the Legal Framework (1982–1997)

1982 — McLellan Joins Dykema

Richard D. McLellan’s private practice merges with Dykema Gossett. He becomes head of the Government Policy & Practice Group and Managing Member of the Lansing office. He had previously served on Gov. William Milliken’s staff.

Source: Wikipedia; McLellan biography, Mackinac Center.

Actor: Richard McLellan (Dykema partner, Lansing)

1987 — McLellan Co-Founds Mackinac Center

McLellan co-founds the Mackinac Center for Public Policy, a free-market think tank that will become the intellectual engine behind Michigan’s charter school movement. He serves as board secretary for decades.

Source: Mackinac Center

Actors: Richard McLellan, Joseph Olson

1988 — Dykema Registers Shelf Nonprofits

Dykema registers pre-formed nonprofit entities — empty corporate shells ready for activation:

EntityLARA IDFiledStatus
Dykema Gossett Nonprofit Shelf Corporation800865335Aug 16, 1988Dissolved
Dykema Gossett Shelf Nonprofit Club Corporation800797761Oct 7, 1988Dissolved

Filed by Cindy M. Wilder at 800 Michigan National Tower, Lansing (Dykema’s former Lansing office). Dissolved within months.

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Entity: Dykema Gossett PLLC

1990 — McLellan Runs Engler Transition

McLellan serves as transition director for Governor-elect John Engler. This positions Dykema at the center of the incoming administration that will create charter schools.

Source: Wikipedia; Mackinac Center biography

Actors: Richard McLellan, John Engler

Oct 5, 1993 — Engler Proposes Charter Schools

Governor Engler proposes charter school legislation in a speech before a joint session of the Michigan Legislature.

Source: Founders Library

Actor: John Engler

Dec 3, 1993 — Dykema Writes the Charter School Law

SB 896, creating Part 6a of the Revised School Code, passes the Legislature. Richard McLellan and Leonard Wolfe of Dykema Gossett are the “leading legal architects” of the legislation.

McLellan personally conducted “12 hours of shuttle diplomacy” in the Senate Majority Leader’s conference room to negotiate a version that would survive constitutional challenge.

The law allows:

  • State universities, community colleges, ISDs, and school districts to authorize charter schools
  • For-profit management companies to operate charter schools
  • A 3% authorization fee (incentivizing authorizers to keep schools open)
  • No statutory authorizer evaluation system
  • Board members appointed without identity disclosure requirements

Source: Founders Library; MI Good Government; Dykema.com Education page

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe (Dykema)

Jan 14, 1994 — Engler Signs PA 362

Governor Engler signs the charter school law. Michigan becomes the 9th state to enact a charter school law.

Source: Founders Library

Actors: John Engler, Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe

1994 — First Charter Schools Open

Central Michigan University becomes the first authorizer. Three schools open: Casa Maria Academy (Detroit), New Branches School (Grand Rapids), Northlane Math and Science Academy.

Source: CMU Center for Charter Schools

1997 — Dykema Defends the Law at Supreme Court

The Michigan Education Association challenges the constitutionality of PA 362. Dykema’s McLellan and Wolfe defend the law before the Michigan Supreme Court in Council of Organizations and Affiliates v. Engler, 455 Mich 557 (1997).

The Court upholds the law and orders state funding restored.

Court record lists: “Dykema, Gossett, P.L.L.C. by Richard D. McLellan, Lori M. Silsbury, and Leonard C. Wolfe, Lansing, for intervening Defendants-Appellants.”

Source: Justia; 455 Mich 557

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe, Lori Silsbury (Dykema)

Phase 2: The Machine Operator Arrives (2009–2016)

2009 — Wilk Forms Larry Deshazor Community Fund

W. Alan Wilk begins his entity formation practice. First documented entity:

EntityLARA IDYear
Larry Deshazor Community Fund70654L2009

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Actor: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema)

2011 — NERD Fund

Wilk serves as legal and compliance officer for Governor Snyder’s NERD Fund (New Energy to Reinvent and Diversify). The fund:

  • Raised $2.19M from undisclosed donors over 3 years
  • Paid Rich Baird’s $100K salary
  • Paid EM Kevyn Orr’s travel expenses
  • Shut down in 2013 after transparency criticism

Source: Detroit News, Nov 19, 2014

Actors: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema), Rick Snyder, Rich Baird, Kevyn Orr

2011 — Wolfe Lifts the Charter Cap

Leonard Wolfe “plays instrumental role” in SB 618 (signed Dec 20, 2011), which phases out the cap on university-authorized charter schools. Wolfe attends the signing ceremony with Governor Snyder.

This removes the 150-school limit that had constrained charter expansion since 1999.

Source: Dykema.com

Actors: Leonard Wolfe (Dykema), Rick Snyder

2012 — Banks Elected to State House; Wells-Stallworth Joins MacDowell Board

Brian Roderick Banks elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (D-Detroit). Serves as Chair of the Detroit Caucus.

Nicole Wells Stallworth appointed to MacDowell Preparatory Academy board. She will serve continuously for 14 years.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; charterschools.org

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth

2015 — Dykema Sues Ellison (Garcia v. Title Check)

Dykema represents the plaintiff in Garcia v. Title Check LLC (1:15-cv-00975, W.D. Michigan). Obtains $73,752.45 in sanctions against attorney Philip L. Ellison for litigation misconduct.

Banks and Ellison were MSU Law classmates (2010).

Source: PACER, W.D. Michigan

Actors: Philip Ellison, Dykema attorneys (unnamed)

Phase 3: Dark Money Pipeline Activates (2016–2021)

Sep 8, 2016 — Wilk Forms Save Detroit Jobs

W. Alan Wilk incorporates Save Detroit Jobs (LARA 802002459). Entity email: compliance@dykema.com. Same day, Wilk also incorporates Detroit Jobs First (per Metro Times, FCC filings).

SDJ board: Rev. James Holley (president, former Duggan civic liaison), Mike Allen (LIUNA Local 1191), Lisa Canada (MI Regional Council of Carpenters).

Both entities are created to fight Proposal A — a citizen-led community benefits ordinance in Detroit.

Source: Michigan LARA; Metro Times

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, James Holley, Mike Allen, Lisa Canada

Nov 2016 — SDJ Pays Carol Banks $14,279; Pays Dykema $9,000

Save Detroit Jobs pays Carol Banks (chief of staff to Councilman Scott Benson) approximately $14,279 via ~70 separate reimbursements.

SDJ also pays Dykema Gossett nearly $9,000 in legal fees.

SDJ raises over $100,000 from: Blue Cross Blue Shield, Turn Around Wayne County PAC (Matthew Moroun’s Central Transport), Schostak Family PAC (Republican). Renae Moore is recordkeeper for Turn Around Wayne County PAC.

Source: Free Press, Sep 22, 2021

Actors: Carol Banks, Scott Benson, W. Alan Wilk, Renae Moore

2017 — Banks Resigns from State House

Banks resigns from the Michigan House as part of a plea deal that allows him to avoid up to 14 years in prison for defrauding a credit union. He is convicted of 8 felonies (later updated to 9 total: 6 felony, 3 misdemeanor).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Actor: Brian Banks

Sep 2018 — Impact Detroit Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Impact Detroit” (LARA record). First persona change.

Source: Michigan LARA, Entity 802002459

2020 — Wilk Forms Our Neighborhoods First

Wilk incorporates Our Neighborhoods First (LARA 802493189). Officers include Keenann Knox (Impact Church), Lorna Thomas (Public Lighting Authority chair, Duggan appointee), Betty Brooks (ex-police commissioner, “dear friend” of Duggan for 30 years).

Renae Moore serves as both Dykema employee AND compliance officer for the Duggan campaign AND recordkeeper for ONF.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Keenann Knox, Renae Moore, Lorna Thomas, Betty Brooks

Aug 10, 2021 — Detroit Leaders Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Detroit Leaders” — one week after Latisha Johnson and Steve Elrick advance to the general election in District 4. Detroit Leaders sends mailers supporting Johnson against Elrick.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick, Keenann Knox, W. Alan Wilk

Aug 25, 2021 — FBI Raids Carol Banks

FBI raids Carol Banks’ East English Village home as part of “Operation Northern Hook” — the public corruption investigation that produced Councilman Andre Spivey’s bribery conviction. Agents seek records on 501(c)(4) organizations and campaign financing.

Source: Free Press, Aug 25, 2021

Actor: Carol Banks

Nov 2021 — Johnson Wins, Elrick Loses

Latisha Johnson defeats journalist Steve Elrick in Detroit District 4. The dark money entity formed by Dykema’s Wilk helped defeat the journalist who covered Banks’s network.

Source: Wayne County election results

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick

Phase 4: The Board Is Captured (2022–2025)

Aug 2022 — Banks Applies for School Administrator Certificate

Ten days after losing his county commissioner race, Banks applies for a school administrator certificate from MDE. Granted the next day (Sep 2, 2022 — school starts Aug 29).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023; MDE records

Actor: Brian Banks

Feb 2022 — MDE Investigates Banks’s Credentials

MDE sends letter to Wells-Stallworth (MacDowell Board Chair) warning that Banks’s employment “may be in violation of the State School Aid Act.” Banks has no valid Michigan teaching credential.

MDE gives the school a procedural loophole rather than enforcing compliance.

Source: MDE FOIA response, Sep 25, 2026

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth, MDE

Jun 2023 — Wells-Stallworth Defends Charter Board Governance

Wells-Stallworth publishes Bridge Michigan op-ed: “Michigan charter school boards ensure financial accountability.” She presides over a board approving 72.67% revenue extraction to Banks’s management LLC.

Appears on MAPSA podcast: “A Charter School Board Member Tells All.”

Source: Bridge Michigan, Jun 9, 2023

Actor: Nicole Wells Stallworth

Jun 2023 — Wilk Forms Put Progress First

Wilk incorporates Put Progress First — a nonprofit backing Duggan’s leadership, signaling a possible gubernatorial bid. Same Dykema formation pattern.

Source: Bridge Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Mike Duggan

Aug 2023 — Free Press “Back to Fool”

M.L. Elrick publishes “Back to Fool” — exposing Banks as an 8-time felon hired as principal of MacDowell. Board members had donated to Banks’s 2022 county commissioner campaign before hiring him.

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Actor: M.L. Elrick, Brian Banks

Nov 2024 — Purpose Group LLC Filed

The Purpose Group, LLC (LARA 803295082) filed November 14, 2024. Sole member: Brian Banks. This is the management company that will receive 72.67% of school revenue.

Source: Michigan LARA

Actors: Brian Banks

Dec 2024 — Michigan Charter Reform Bills

Michigan legislature passes charter reform requiring authorizers to review contracts over $100K, attend 50%+ of board meetings, and mandate audited EMO financials. This legislation is directly responsive to governance failures like Banks’s operation.

Source: Chalkbeat, Dec 13, 2024

Jan 2025 — FBI Closes Carol Banks Investigation

FBI closes the public corruption investigation into Scott Benson and Janée Ayers without charges. Carol Banks is not charged.

Source: Free Press, Jan 17, 2025

Actor: Carol Banks

2025 — Purpose Charter Academy Authorized

DPSCD authorizes Purpose Charter Academy, citing “claimed improvement” at MacDowell. PCA board assembled:

PositionNameInstitutional Conflict
ChairJudge Cylenthia MillerWayne County 3rd Circuit — former Dykema attorney
Vice ChairLamar MorelandAsst Attorney General — AG could investigate Banks
SecretaryLatisha JohnsonDetroit City Council — Council oversees DPSCD
TreasurerDevin HutchingsFormer SuperPAC co-chair (Michigan Deserves Better)
Asst TreasurerMajor CloraCEO, Clora Funeral Home

Johnson was elected with help from Detroit Leaders — the Dykema-formed entity. Miller is a former Dykema attorney. The board that governs a convicted felon’s school was ASSEMBLED using Dykema infrastructure.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; DPSCD board minutes (Jul 2025); Chalkbeat, Sep 8, 2025

2025 — SDJ Funds Sheffield Mayoral Campaign

SDJ sends $84,500 to Detroit Next PAC, which runs $212,600+ in pro-Sheffield advertising. Sheffield wins. Appoints Chief Bettison (who sits on DPSA board — another charter school board).

Source: TransparencyUSA; campaign finance filings

Actors: Mary Sheffield, Todd Bettison

Phase 5: The Investigation (2026)

Mar 2026 — Miller Announces PCA Board Role

Judge Miller publicly announces her role as PCA Board Chair on LinkedIn: “I am so honored and proud to serve as the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of this amazing new school.”

Source: LinkedIn

Actor: Cylenthia Miller

Sep–Oct 2026 — Investigation Goes Live

  • Sep 13: Clutch Justice publishes MacDowell investigation
  • Sep 21: FOIA filed with MDE
  • Sep 25: MDE responds confirming credential investigation
  • Oct 4: AGC complaints filed (Miller, Moreland)
  • Oct 5: JTC supplements filed (Miller, Yancey)
  • Oct 7: NHT scan discovers Wilk entity network
  • Oct 8: Dykema infrastructure page published on detroit.primals.eco
  • Oct 9: This chronology compiled

Source: detroit.primals.eco evidence library; clutchjustice.com

The Pattern

1988: Dykema registers shelf nonprofits
1993: Dykema writes the charter school law (PA 362)
1994: First charter schools open under the law
1997: Dykema defends the law at Michigan Supreme Court
2011: Dykema lifts the charter cap (unlimited schools)
2011: Dykema attorney Wilk runs Snyder's NERD Fund
2016: Wilk forms dark money vehicles (SDJ, DJF)
2016: SDJ pays Carol Banks $14K, pays Dykema $9K
2017: Banks convicted — resigns from state house
2021: SDJ (as Detroit Leaders) defeats journalist Elrick
2021: FBI raids Carol Banks for dark money records
2022: Banks hired at MacDowell (no valid credential)
2023: Free Press exposes Banks — nothing happens
2024: Purpose Group LLC formed by Banks
2025: PCA board assembled — includes Dykema's former associate (Miller)
      and Dykema's dark money beneficiary (Johnson)
2025: SDJ funds Sheffield mayoral campaign ($84K → $212K ads)
2026: Investigation publishes the connection

One law firm. 36 years. From authoring the charter school law to staffing the board of a convicted felon’s school via dark money.

Every entry on this page resolves to a public record.

Verify

SDJ campaign financeWayne County Clerk — search “Save Detroit Jobs”

All sources are public records, published court opinions, campaign finance filings, and the firm’s own website and press releases. Every date, entity, and actor can be independently verified.

entry.title: There's a Leak in the Dyke
entry.content:
On February 26, 2025, a compliance specialist named Renae Moore took the witness stand in Ingham County District Court. She was the first witness called in the preliminary examination of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield, who faces 13 felony charges including embezzlement and conspiracy.

Moore works for Dykema Gossett PLLC, the law firm headquartered at 201 Townsend Street in Lansing — across the street from the Michigan State Capitol.

Under oath, she testified to three things that should concern every person in this state.

1. 80+ Accounts. One Desk.

Moore testified that at Dykema, she helps manage more than 80+ accounts — political nonprofit funds tied to Michigan lawmakers and officials.

She was the assistant secretary/treasurer of the Peninsula Fund, Chatfield’s political nonprofit that raised $1.8 million from anonymous donors between 2018 and 2020 while he served as House Speaker.

When asked by Judge Molly Hennessey Greenwalt whether she had a duty to report concerns about problematic spending — including a strip club tab submitted as a business expense — Moore replied:

“No. Not that I am aware of.”

Chatfield’s defense attorney, Mary Chartier, said to Moore on the stand:

“This entire time, Dykema is getting paid to ensure the Peninsula Fund is compliant.”

Moore testified there were times the fund was not compliant with the law.

Sources: Bridge Michigan, Detroit News, Lansing State Journal, AG Affidavit

2. Both Parties. Same Person. Same Title.

During cross-examination, Chartier highlighted that Moore holds the same title — assistant treasurer/secretary — on another political nonprofit: the Promise to the People Fund.

That fund is affiliated with Attorney General Dana Nessel.

The same Attorney General whose office is prosecuting Chatfield.

One compliance specialist. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. Same desk. Same role. Same firm.

Source: Publicly available tax filings; Moore’s testimony and court documents, per Lansing State Journal.

3. The Firm Across the Street

Craig Mauger of the Detroit News wrote the sentence that explains everything:

“Dykema, which has a law office across the street from the state Capitol, handles the paperwork and tax filings of many of the politician-connected nonprofits.”

80+ accounts. Both parties. One building. One switchboard: 517-374-9100 .

What Else Does This Firm Do?

Dykema’s own website states:

“Dykema has been a leader in structural educational reform since authoring charter school legislation in the early 1990s, successfully defending the legislation’s legal challenges, and representing state universities in establishing and overseeing public school academies in the last 20 years.”

They wrote the law that created Michigan’s charter school system. Then they defended that law in court. Then they represented the state universities that authorize charter schools. Then their partners formed charter entities by the hundreds through the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs.

And their political compliance team — the same team where Moore manages 80+ accounts — runs the PAC compliance for the dark money vehicles that influence who sits on those charter school boards.

The Vehicles

W. Alan Wilk is Dykema’s Political Compliance Team Leader. He has been with the firm since passing the Michigan Bar in 1995. His phone number is 517-374-9122. Moore’s is 517-374-9121. One digit apart. Same desk cluster.

Wilk has incorporated at least 7+ dark money vehicles through LARA:

#EntityPurposeYear
1Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit LeadersDetroit City Council races2016
2Our Neighborhoods FirstAnti-community benefits agreement2016
3Detroit Jobs FirstDetroit ballot measures2016
4RFFW LLCAbortion ballot committee ( $1,000,000 )2022
5Turn Around Wayne County PACWayne County racesongoing
6Put Progress FirstPro-Duggan governor campaign2023
7Michigan First PrinciplesAnti-John James attack ads2025

Save Detroit Jobs spent $84,000 defeating a sitting council member and electing his replacement — who then joined the board of a charter school run by a superintendent with 9 criminal convictions.

Put Progress First spent $545,000 supporting Mike Duggan’s independent governor campaign. Then Michigan First Principles spent money attacking John James, Duggan’s Republican rival in the governor’s race. Both formed by Wilk. Same attorney. Same desk. Opposite missions.

The Dykema Federal PAC (FEC ID: C00342113) gave $4,000 to Barrett and $4,000 to John James in the same cycle that Wilk’s vehicle was attacking James.

The firm funds the candidate AND the attack on the candidate.

Sources: LARA entity search, TransparencyUSA, FEC, Bridge Detroit, Detroit News

The Co-Billing

In 2017, FOIA records showed that Dykema billed the State of Michigan $108,238 for the teacher 3% retirement case under Governor Snyder. Five attorneys worked on it. Two of them:

  • W. Alan Wilk — $433.50/hour (dark money architect)
  • Jason Hanselman — $374/hour (charter entity formation)

The attorney who forms dark money vehicles and the attorney who forms charter school entities work the same cases and bill the state together.

Source: MLive, FOIA records

The Revolving Door

Aaron Keel was the Assistant Director of Government Relations for the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB), where he lobbied for charter school oversight and accountability. MASB’s official position calls for “accountability and transparency of the authorizers and management companies.”

Then Keel became Deputy Chief of Staff in the Michigan House Democratic Caucus. Then Director of Legislative Affairs at the Michigan Department of Treasury. Then, in 2023, he joined Dykema as a government policy advisor — now working at the firm whose clients the MASB oversight legislation would regulate.

He went from lobbying for charter school accountability to working at the firm that built the charter school infrastructure.

Source: Dykema, MASB Resolutions

Five Levels

Count the roles one firm plays in one system:

  1. Wrote the charter school law (1990s)
  2. Defended the law in court (constitutional challenges)
  3. Represents the authorizers (state universities)
  4. Forms the entities under the law (LARA filings, hundreds)
  5. Runs the PAC compliance that elects the board members (Wilk/Moore: SDJ → council → charter school board)

No other entity in Michigan occupies every level of the same regulatory system.

The Leak

The Dutch have a story about a boy who put his finger in a leaking dyke to save his village. The story is American fiction — invented by Phoebe Cary in 1865. In reality, when Dutch dykes leak, they don’t trickle. Whole sections give way. You don’t stop it with a finger. You stop it with a boat.

Moore’s testimony is the leak.

One compliance specialist. 80+ accounts. No duty to report. Both parties. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. Strip club tabs submitted as business expenses. Policy manuals written by the firm and ignored by the clients. And when asked under oath if she had any obligation to tell anyone:

“No. Not that I am aware of.”

The dyke is leaking.

Every claim in this article is sourced to sworn testimony, published news reports, FOIA records, FEC filings, LARA entity records, or the firm’s own public website. No anonymous sources. No allegations. Public record.

entry.title: The Corporate Network — LARA Entity Analysis
entry.content:
How to Read This Page

Every entity listed below is a public record in the Michigan LARA Business Entity Search. Entity IDs are provided so anyone can verify. Officer names, addresses, and filing dates come directly from LARA annual reports and formation documents — all public records under Michigan law.

We focus on business addresses and registered agent addresses (which are legally required to be public for service of process). We do not publish residential addresses for peripheral individuals.

Source notation: “LARA [Entity ID]” means the data comes from Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs business entity filings. You can verify any entity by searching mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us with the Entity ID number.

The Purpose Empire — Three Entities, One Man

Brian Banks controls three “Purpose”-branded entities. Together they form the corporate infrastructure for his charter school operation.

EntityLARA IDTypeFiledStatusAgent
Purpose Charter Academy900072324Nonprofit Corp07/31/2025ActiveBrian Banks
The Purpose Group, LLC803295082LLC11/14/2024ActiveBrian Banks
Purpose Foundation803294855Nonprofit Corp12/09/2024ActiveBrian Banks

Purpose Charter Academy is registered at 10101 E. Canfield, Detroit MI 48214 — the school address. The Purpose Group LLC is registered at the same address. Purpose Foundation is registered at Banks’s personal address.

The PCA Board of Directors (LARA Filing)

This is the board that governs a charter school serving Detroit’s children:

OfficerTitleSignificance
Cylenthia Latoye MillerPresident, DirectorIdentity under investigation
Latisha JohnsonSecretaryDetroit City Council Member (District 2). Her election was supported by Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders — the dark money vehicle that fought the journalist exposing Banks. See below.
Devin HutchingsTreasurerOwns DB Strategies LLC and DB Athletics LLC (LARA 802710175, 802715414). Based in Ypsilanti, not Detroit.
Major CloraDirectorPreviously operated American Motor Coach Inc (LARA 800526511, dissolved).
Lamar MorelandDirectorBanks’s current litigation attorney. Moreland represents Banks in civil proceedings. He is simultaneously a director of Banks’s charter school. This dual role — attorney and board member — raises conflict of interest concerns under MRPC 1.7.

Banks is the registered agent but does not appear as a named officer. He controls the entity through agent status while the board provides institutional cover.

Banks’s Full Entity Portfolio — Twelve Entities

A search of LARA records by registered agent reveals Banks controls or has controlled twelve business entities across Michigan:

Banks uses multiple email addresses across filings: BanksStrategy@gmail.com, BrianBanksJD@gmail.com, BBesq06@aol.com, and brian@anchorrockservices.com.

The initials “JD” and “esq” appear in two of these emails despite Banks never being admitted to any state bar. His felony convictions prevented bar admission after earning his J.D. from Michigan State University.

The Three-Named Dark Money Vehicle

Save Detroit Jobs is a single nonprofit corporation operating under three different names:

NameRegistration DateExpiration
Save Detroit Jobs09/08/2016 (original filing)—
Impact Detroit09/07/2018 (assumed name)12/31/2028
Detroit Leaders08/10/2021 (assumed name)12/31/2026

LARA Entity ID: 802002459. All three names are registered on the same entity.

Who formed it: The registered agent is The Corporation Company (a professional formation service). The mailing address is 201 Townsend Street, Suite 900, Lansing MI 48933 — the office of Dykema Gossett PLLC, Michigan’s largest law firm. The entity email is compliance@dykema.com.

Michigan’s largest law firm set up the dark money vehicle that was used to fight journalists reporting on Banks’s network.

Officers — All at One Address

Damian MitchellTreasurer, Director13560 E. McNichols, Detroit 48205
Elisha BrownSecretary, Director13560 E. McNichols, Detroit 48205

All three officers list the same address. Kenneth Daniels is separately the agent on 15 other business entities, primarily in real estate and construction (Daniels Realty Group, KANDICO Construction, DANCOM Properties, and others).

What Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders Did

In 2021, operating as “Detroit Leaders,” this entity funded the campaign of Latisha Johnson against incumbent Steve Elrick — the journalist who had reported extensively on Banks’s network. Johnson won. She is now Secretary on the PCA board (see above).

The 12-step suppression loop: Banks’s network → funds dark money vehicle → dark money vehicle fights journalist → journalist loses election → replacement (Johnson) joins Banks’s school board.

Right Turn Project — The Dissolved Charity and the Money Loop

The Right Turn Project Inc (LARA 800936257) was a nonprofit corporation filed May 7, 2013. It was dissolved by operation of law on December 1, 2021 — meaning LARA dissolved it for failure to file annual reports.

OfficerTitleAddress

Terrence TarverSecretary, Director16500 North Park Dr, Southfield 48075

The entity email was BBesq06@aol.com — which is Banks’s personal email, not Holland’s. Banks controlled the entity through Holland.

The Ross Catering Money Loop

Carlton Ross was simultaneously:

  1. Treasurer of the Right Turn Project (a charity receiving PAC transfers)
  2. Connected to Ross Catering — the vendor paid $35,000+ by Banks’s political campaigns

LARA records show two Ross Catering entities: Ross Catering Company Inc (800646584, agent: Louis Ross, dissolved 2024) and Ross Catering Events of Excellence LLC (801351679, agent: Gwendolyn Lewis, active). The relationship between Carlton Ross, Louis Ross, and Gwendolyn Lewis requires further investigation, but the structural pattern is clear: money flows from PAC → charity (where Ross is treasurer) → catering company (where Ross has connections).

The 16500 North Park Address

Carlton Ross and Terrence Tarver both list 16500 North Park Drive, Southfield MI 48075 as their address on the Right Turn Project filing.

Banks’s dissolved entity B. Roderick’s Salon & Spa (LARA 800591240, filed 2001) was registered at 16500 Northpark Dr #1715, Southfield MI 48075 — the same building. Banks used this address a decade before Ross and Tarver appeared there.

Inner Link Graphics — The $98,000 Print Vendor

The Inner Link LLC (LARA 801470477) received $98,291 from Banks-connected political committees. LARA records reveal:

Thomas also owns The Larry Thomas Group LLC (LARA 801763084, filed 2014), a separate entity at a different Southfield address.

The political print vendor also runs an obituary printing website. $98,291 for one vendor across six committees.

Custom Promotions — The Dissolve-and-Reform Attorney

Custom Promotions appears in two LARA incarnations:

EntityLARA IDAgentFiledStatus

The Inc was dissolved in February 2022. The LLC was filed three months later in May 2022 with the same name. Officers of the original entity: Jason Gordon (President), Sara Gordon (Treasurer), Eric Gordon (Secretary). A family business passed from father to son via dissolve-and-reform.

Jason Samuel Gordon is an attorney. He owns Deen Legal Services PLLC (LARA 801895172, filed 2009) at the same address as Custom Promotions LLC: 14326 East 9 Mile Road, Warren MI 48089. His email: JGordon@DeenLegal.com.

Gordon was investigated by the FBI, IRS, and Department of Labor in connection with the UAW bribery case — over $3 million in payments from the UAW. Custom Promotions also received payments from Latisha Johnson’s campaign.

Gordon is agent on 20+ entities including real estate LLCs, marketing companies, and his law firm — all while under federal investigation.

The Endorsement Machine — Four Eastside Slates

The “Eastside Slate” endorsement operation has been filed as a LARA entity four separate times:

IncarnationLARA IDFiledAgentStatus

Original Eastside Slate80243449804/09/2020Carol BanksActive

Carol Banks — Brian Banks’s sister, a former Chief of Staff to Council Member Benson, and an FBI investigation target — currently controls the only active version.

Spencer Leach — The Political Machine Builder

W. Spencer Leach filed 13 political and nonprofit entities, many batch-filed on the same day with consecutive LARA Entity IDs:

Filed 04/28/2008 (consecutive IDs):

  • Eastside Slate (800916317)
  • Eastside Community Slate (800916318)
  • Michigan Black Democrats (800916316)

Filed 05/15/2015 (near-consecutive IDs):

  • Detroit Democratic Club (800938179)
  • Detroit Democrat Club (800938180)
  • Democratic Progressive Alliance (800938181)

Filing three to four political organizations on the same day with consecutive Entity IDs is the hallmark of manufactured political infrastructure — organizations created not to represent constituencies but to control endorsement pipelines.

Parallel Pan-African Naming

Carol Banks and Spencer Leach use matching entity naming conventions drawn from Pan-African geography:

Carol BanksSpencer Leach
The Niger Group (800934647)The Songhai Group (801659651)

Same officers appear across both operators’ entities. Beverly Nakenge serves as Treasurer on both Carol Banks’s Original Eastside Slate and Niger Group. Kiambu Elcock serves as Director/Secretary on both.

The Law Firms — A Family Connection?

Great Lakes Legal Group PLLC (LARA 802112914)

FieldDetail

Crump-Gibson is also a Hearing Panelist for the Michigan Attorney Discipline Board — the body that processes attorney grievance complaints.

Crump Hall of Justice Law Firm PLLC

Verkeydia Hall — the attorney who filed a PPO petition against Kevin Mok — owns a separate law firm called Crump Hall of Justice Law Firm (website: mychoj.com, email: vhall@chojlf.com). The firm name contains “Crump” — Hall’s maiden name.

Her MSU email is crumpver@msu.edu. Crump-Gibson attended MSU for undergrad.

Both Crump-Gibson and Crump Hall share the surname Crump. Both attended Michigan State University. Both represent Brian Banks. If they are related, Banks’s legal representation has been a family operation.

Hall is also listed as Board Director of MacDowell Preparatory Academy on the school’s official website (macdowellprep.com/board-of-directors/). Banks’ attorney’s probable relative sits on the board of Banks’ school.

CitizenDetroit Action Group — The Board Overlap

EIN 82-2361291 (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer). CEO: Sheila Cockrel (former Detroit City Council member).

Crump-Gibson served as Vice Chair, then Chair, of the CitizenDetroit Action Group board. The same board includes Hon. Misha Stallworth as a Director.

The Stallworth dynasty (all public record, documented on this site):

These problems originate in dynasties, move through entities, and land on humans. The board overlap does not imply that Crump-Gibson knew about the Stallworth family’s role in installing Banks. It means the social graph through which Banks finds legal representation is the same social graph through which charter school authorization flows.

Correlation does not imply causation. But causation can be masked — and hidden — by correlation.

Within 24 hours of entering Banks’ case, Crump-Gibson voluntarily limited her scope in writing, declining law enforcement and PPO matters. That is a written record of an attorney drawing an ethical line. The correspondence timeline documents the full sequence.

Each person at GLLG can choose which side of the demarcation they are on. As of this writing, the scope limitation suggests the choice is being made carefully.

WhitlowBanks LLC (LARA 802085022)

Filed 04/20/2017 during Banks’s political career. Agent: Tameka Ramsey (Pontiac, MI). The entity name literally combines “Whitlow” and “Banks.” TransparencyUSA records show “Carles Whitlow” received $8,500 as a payee from Banks’s Senate campaign — the 5th largest individual payee.

LARA Compliance Issues

The following are potential compliance issues under Michigan’s business entity statutes, identified from public LARA filings. These are questions — not accusations. The appropriate bodies to investigate are LARA, the Attorney General’s Charitable Trust Section, and the IRS.

1. Annual Report Failures (MCL 450.2911 / MCL 450.4207)

Multiple entities in the network have “Not Good” standing for failure to file annual reports, including entities that received or disbursed political funds:

EntityStandingAnnual Report DueStatus
Right Turn ProjectNot Good10/01/2019Dissolved (12/01/2021)
Banks Powerwashing LLCNot Good—Inactive since 2016
Free Flow Gutter ProtectionNot Good—Inactive since 2026
Ross Catering Events of ExcellenceNot Good—Inactive since 2010
Detroiters for Good GovernmentNot Good—Inactive since 2020

2. Nonprofit Self-Dealing (MCL 450.2545a)

The Right Turn Project’s Treasurer (Carlton Ross) is connected to the vendor (Ross Catering) that received campaign payments. Michigan Nonprofit Corporation Act § 545a requires that transactions involving a director’s or officer’s financial interest be disclosed and approved by disinterested directors. There is no indication this occurred.

3. Dissolved Entity Operations

The Right Turn Project was dissolved December 1, 2021. Under MCL 450.2831, dissolved corporations may only wind up affairs and liquidate assets — they may not conduct new business. Any transactions after dissolution raise compliance questions.

4. Convicted Felon as Nonprofit Officer

Joseph Holland (MDOC #443789, convicted cocaine dealer) served as President and Registered Agent of the Right Turn Project and currently serves as Treasurer and Secretary of Purpose Foundation. While Michigan law does not categorically prohibit convicted felons from serving as nonprofit officers, organizations receiving public funds or serving vulnerable populations (children) face additional scrutiny.

5. Unauthorized Practice of Law Concerns

Banks operated Serenity Guardianship Services Inc (LARA 802290962) as a for-profit corporation from 2019-2023, serving as sole officer. Guardianship work in Michigan involves petitioning courts, managing wards’ legal rights, and filing accountings — activities that constitute the practice of law under MCL 450.681. Banks was never admitted to any bar.

6. Entity Formation Patterns

The dissolve-and-reform pattern (Custom Promotions Inc dissolved February 2022 → Custom Promotions LLC filed May 2022) may be used to shed liabilities while maintaining brand continuity. The three-name dark money vehicle (Save Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders) allows the same entity to operate under different public identities for different audiences.

How to Verify

Every entity on this page can be verified at Michigan LARA Business Entity Search:

  1. Go to the search page
  2. Enter the Entity ID number in the search field
  3. Select “Entity ID” as the search type
  4. All officer names, addresses, filing dates, and assumed names are publicly displayed

This is not a dossier. It is an index of public records with analysis of what those records reveal when connected.

Related

  • Data Braid — GLLG Entity Graph — Six independent database searches converge on one social graph. The braid method.
  • Institutional Capture Graph — Full network visualization with 98 nodes and 160 edges.

All data sourced from Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) public business entity filings, ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (IRS 990 filings), school board websites, and State Bar / LinkedIn records. Entity IDs and EINs provided for independent verification. Analysis reflects patterns observable in public records as of October 9, 2026.
